items.readable_text:
Content:
We can use area models to represent division problems involving three-digit numbers.

Content:
Let's consider the area model below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/588a30c846eb03562d5d4edf2273d337]

Content:
To determine the missing length, we consider the area of the yellow rectangle (the one on the left-hand side).

Content:
The area of the yellow rectangle is [MATH: 320,] and its width is [MATH: 4.] Hence, the length of this rectangle must be
[MATH: 320\div 4.]

Content:
To carry out this division, we write [MATH: 320] as a product with [MATH: 10] as one of the factors and then swap the order of multiplication and division:

Content:
[MATH: 320 ÷ 4|=; 32 × 10 ÷ 4|=; 32 ÷ 4 × 10|=; (32 ÷ 4) × 10|=; 8 × 10|=; 80]

Content:
We can now add this length to the area model.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/6eda76779dd8fd772054b8e573b06b75]
